hasPart.name: Recognizing a Layer 2 forwarding loop
hasPart.text: A redundant physical link can be part of a healthy topology. A loop exists when the forwarding paths form a cycle for the same VLAN. Repeated copies of a broadcast and a stationary endpoint’s MAC address moving between switch ports are clues. Trace the active paths to confirm the cycle.

hasPart.name: Verifying the STP root bridge
hasPart.text: Within one instance, the switch with the lowest bridge identifier wins the election. With equal effective priorities, the lower bridge MAC address wins. A newly elected root can change which links forward while the topology remains loop-free.

hasPart.name: Interpreting spanning-tree port roles and states
hasPart.text: A root port leads toward the root bridge. A designated port serves its segment. In RSTP, alternate and backup ports provide redundant paths and normally discard user traffic. Classic STP distinguishes blocking, listening, learning, forwarding and disabled. RSTP groups the nonlearning, nonforwarding conditions under discarding. A learning port records source MAC addresses before it forwards user frames.

citation.name: RFC 4188 §4, dot1dStpPortState and classic spanning-tree port states

hasPart.name: Diagnosing an incorrect access VLAN
hasPart.text: When a switch accepts untagged frames from a workstation, the port’s configured VLAN determines where those frames enter the switched network. If each VLAN has its own IPv4 subnet and DHCP scope, a lease from an unexpected subnet is a clue. Compare the port’s assigned VLAN and the lease with the network plan.

citation.name: RFC 4363 §5, dot1qPvid and VLAN classification of untagged frames

hasPart.name: Tracing an ACL decision
hasPart.text: Identify the interface and traffic direction, then follow the policy’s evaluation order. In a first-match ACL, a rule that drops all traffic from a subnet also drops its web traffic, even if a later rule permits that service. For a packet that matches no entry, check the policy’s default action. Where counters are available, compare rule counts before and after a test.
